sentences.show: 36 barrels of gunpowder sat under Parliament. One letter gave them away.
The Gunpowder Plot was foiled on this day in 1605.
Catholic plotters, led by Robert Catesby, planned to blow up the king.
They took a cellar under the House of Lords, and filled it with gunpowder.
Guarding it: Guy Fawkes, posing as a servant called John Johnson.
Ten days before, a Catholic lord got an anonymous letter.
"They shall receive a terrible blow this Parliament," it warned.
The plotters heard about it, and decided it was a hoax.
Late that night, guards searched the cellar, and found Fawkes, with a lantern, slow matches, and the barrels.
The king ordered him tortured. His signature shows what it did.
That night, London lit bonfires. Britain still does, every 5th of November.
Also on this day: the Battle of Inkerman was fought in fog, and India sent a probe to Mars.
